parsed.study_design: Exploratory mixed-methods typical-case study using cross-sectional semi-structured household interviews
parsed.population_and_sample: Adult household heads or spouses in two census tracts in São Gonçalo, Rio de Janeiro: 45 households in lower-income Jardim Catarina and 46 households in higher-income Mutondo, representing 25% of households in each selected tract.
parsed.exposure: Residence in socioeconomically contrasting neighborhoods served through unequal institutional and infrastructural arrangements of the municipal public water-distribution system, including differences in storage capacity, pressure, continuity, metering, and service provision.
parsed.outcome: Household water connection and actual availability, including supply frequency and interruptions, pressure, shortages, sufficiency for domestic needs, reliance on alternative sources and pumps, payment burden, and perceived water security.
parsed.rationale: The verification-method section (pp. 6–9) reports an identifiable exploratory mixed-methods design comparing two connected neighborhoods and administering semi-structured questionnaires to 91 households. Results (pp. 9–14) provide empirical access outcomes, including only 15.5% receiving daily water and nearly 90% reporting routine shortages in Jardim Catarina, versus 95.6% receiving daily water and 90% reporting that water never ran out in Mutondo. The discussion and final remarks (pp. 14–18) connect these disparities to governance and institutional factors, including unequal service provision, infrastructure and storage choices, deficient official access indicators, public policy, and regulation.
